sources.entry: TICS - Menu bar app that plays mechanical keyboard sounds as you type, and mouse sounds as you click, drag and scroll.

summary.one_liner: TICS is a macOS menu bar app that plays mechanical keyboard sounds as you type and mouse sounds as you click, drag and scroll.
keywords: make typing sound like a keyboard
summary.what_it_does: TICS runs in the menu bar and plays a keyboard sound for every key you press in any app, using one of 11 keyboard sound packs (such as Cherry MX Blue, Holy Panda, Topre Purple) or a synthetic one generated in code. You can vary the pitch per keystroke, set different sounds for press and release, and assign custom sounds or per-key pitch and volume in Set Up Keyboard. Mouse clicks, dragging (ratchet-style, speed-dependent) and scroll-wheel notches also make sounds, adjustable in Mouse Settings. A Logitech tile can add sounds for buttons that Logi Options+ takes over. TICS lowers its volume to 40% while other audio is playing. It checks GitHub once a day for new versions and can be set not to connect at all.
use_cases: make typing sound like a mechanical keyboard
add click sounds to mouse actions on a Mac
assign custom sound files to keys or shortcuts
audio feedback while typing for focus or enjoyment
hear mouse drags and scroll clicks on macOS
how_to_run: Download the .dmg from the project's releases, open it and drag TICS to Applications (requires macOS 14 or later)
bun run dev (build from source: debug build, then opens the app)
bun run build (release build at build/Tics.app)
notable: Mouse clicks and the synthetic keyboard sounds are generated on the fly rather than from audio files
Auto-lowers volume to 40% while music, video or calls play, using macOS reported audio usage without needing extra permission
Privacy-focused: listens only for key presses, never saves typed text or click locations
Optional Logitech tile with MX Master 4 button haptic feedback
caveats: Requires Input Monitoring permission on macOS; Logitech tile additionally requires Bluetooth permission
Without a Apple Development certificate, the app is signed ad hoc and macOS asks for permission again after every build
Requires macOS 14 or later and Swift 6 to build from source
